chunks.text: We used median frequency balancing as presented in [26]. The weight assigned to each class is equal to the median of all class frequencies divided by class frequency. This balancing results in the larger classes having weights smaller than 1 and the smaller classes are having weights larger than 1. The unlabelled pixels are ignored during training. Since the convolutions in the encoder network are identical to VGG16, the encoder weights are initialized using VGG16 pre-trained weights on the ImageNet classiﬁcation challenge dataset. The decoder weights are initialized according to [27]. The encoder-decoder network is trained using the modular training technique presented in [28]. First, the outermost encoder-decoder pair is trained. Then, deeper pairs are added and trained one by one while the weights of the preceding pairs remain ﬁxed. The training is using stochastic gradient descent optimization with learning rate equal to 10−2. During the training of each pair, learning rate scheduling is applied. The implemented scheduler reads training loss values after each epoch, and if no improvement is seen for 10 epochs, the learning rate is reduced to 10−3. Next time the training loss shows no improvement for 10 epochs the training of that pair is stopped, and the next encoder-decoder pair is added and trained. This training approach requires approximately 680 epochs for the training of the whole network. A RCHITECTURE SegNet architecture, illustrated in Fig. 1, consists of en- coder network, corresponding decoder network, and soft- max classiﬁer. The proposed topology for encoder network corresponds to the ﬁrst 13 convolutional layers of VGG16 network. Therefore, it is possible to initialize the encoder net- work with pre-trained weights for large datasets. The encoder network is followed by the decoder network with the same number of convolutional layers. The ﬁnal soft-max layer produces class probabilities for each pixel independently. Each encoder layer in the network consists of convolu- tions, batch normalization and ReLU non-linearity, followed by non-overlapping max-pooling layer (2 × 2 window and stride 2). R ELATED WORK In recent years, semantic pixel-wise segmentation gained signiﬁcant attention from machine learning researchers. Ac- curate and efﬁcient image segmentation is needed in many core computer vision problems, such as autonomous driving, medical sciences, human-machine interaction, image search engines and augmented reality [13]. Many segmentation architectures are inspired by the con- tributions and success of standard architectures like AlexNet [14], GoogLeNet [15], VGG [16], and ResNet[17]. The Fully Convolutional Network (FCN) presented in [9] is consid- ered a breakthrough in deep learning based semantic seg- mentation. Unlike previously mentioned architectures, FCNs consists of convolutional layers without any fully-connected layers. Pixel-wise prediction and recovery of spatial informa- tion are achieved by upsampling using deconvolutions. The important feature of FCNs is their ability to make pixel-wise predictions for inputs of arbitrary size [9]. SegNet is an efﬁcient encoder-decoder neural network for pixel-wise segmentation. The encoder network in SegNet is topologically identical to the convolutional layers in VGG16 and without fully connected layers. The key component of SegNet is the decoder network that uses a set of decoders each corresponding to one encoder. Unlike architectures that store the full encoder network feature maps, SegNet only stores the max-pooling indices of the feature maps and uses them in its decoder network for upsampling. The storing of indices provides good performance and efﬁciency in terms of memory and computational time. Compared with other relevant architectures, SegNets perform competitively on well-known datasets and are one of the best models for solving scene segmentation problems[8]. The U-Net [10], initially proposed for biomedical image segmentation, is a fully convolutional encoder-decoder net- work with symmetric architecture. Unlike SegNet, U-Net stores entire feature maps. The upsampled decoder features are concatenated with corresponding high resolution encoder feature maps for better localization. DeconvNet [11] encoder consists of convolutional layers and two fully connected layers of VGG16. Compared to SegNet, DeconvNet have a larger number of parameters and longer training and inference time. In agriculture, image segmentation has been applied in solving a wide range of tasks related to precision farming, automation and autonomy. One of the applications is the detection of ﬁeld boundaries. In [18], a deep convolutional neural network for semantic segmentation, ResUNet, is used for ﬁeld boundary extraction from satellite images. The study presented in [19] used DeepLabv3+ architecture to classify and extract crop areas from high spatial resolution remote sensing images. The vehicle’s ability to perceive and understand its envi- ronment relies heavily on the processing of visual inputs. The recent success of deep learning architectures for image classiﬁcation, semantic segmentation, and object detection inspired application of deep learning in scene perception for autonomous vehicles. Semantic pixel-wise segmentation is an important part of the scene perception task. The goal of semantic segmentation is to annotate each pixel within an image with a semantically interpretable class from a predeﬁned set of classes. This annotation helps achieve a detailed description of the object boundaries and better understanding of the spatial relationship between different structures present in the scene. This research work aims to advance the real-life appli- cation of semantic segmentation in scene perception for the agricultural environment. The SegNet encoder-decoder architecture [8] is applied in solving the segmentation task. This architecture was selected due to its practical advantages. Compared to architectures presented in [9] and [10], SegNet provides a memory-efﬁcient storing of information from encoder feature maps by using only max-pooling indices. The work presented in [11] uses a similar technique for upsampling in the decoder network, but it has a signiﬁcantly larger number of parameters. Moreover, SegNet is a fully convolutional network and can therefore take input images of arbitrary size. To the best of our knowledge, SegNet architecture has not been applied before in solving scene segmentation task for agricultural vehicles. The main barrier in transferring semantic pixel-wise seg- mentation architectures to agriculture is limited availability of labelled datasets [12]. Therefore, an important contribu- tion of our work is training and performance evaluation of the segmentation network on a new image dataset collected speciﬁcally for the agricultural domain. The images were collected during tractor’s operation in the crop ﬁeld and represent a realistic scenario for driving in the agricultural environment. The dataset contains ﬁve labelled classes of ﬁeld structures: “Vegetation”, “Grass”, “Ground”, “Crop ﬁeld”, and “Obstacle”. Moreover, we present an approach for continuous quali- tative validation of the network in practice. The approach is based on a tool for real-time visualization of segmentation results for images captured by the vehicle’s camera during 2020 16th International Conference on Control, Automation, Robotics and Vision (ICARCV) December 13-15, 2020. chunks.text: We used median frequency balancing as presented in [26]. The weight assigned to each class is equal to the median of all class frequencies divided by class frequency. This balancing results in the larger classes having weights smaller than 1 and the smaller classes are having weights larger than 1. The unlabelled pixels are ignored during training. Since the convolutions in the encoder network are identical to VGG16, the encoder weights are initialized using VGG16 pre-trained weights on the ImageNet classiﬁcation challenge dataset. The decoder weights are initialized according to [27]. The encoder-decoder network is trained using the modular training technique presented in [28]. First, the outermost encoder-decoder pair is trained. Then, deeper pairs are added and trained one by one while the weights of the preceding pairs remain ﬁxed. The training is using stochastic gradient descent optimization with learning rate equal to 10−2. During the training of each pair, learning rate scheduling is applied. The implemented scheduler reads training loss values after each epoch, and if no improvement is seen for 10 epochs, the learning rate is reduced to 10−3. Next time the training loss shows no improvement for 10 epochs the training of that pair is stopped, and the next encoder-decoder pair is added and trained. This training approach requires approximately 680 epochs for the training of the whole network. The work presented in [24] introduces DeepAnomaly, an algorithm that combines deep learning and anomaly detection for the detection of occluded and unknown objects in the agricultural environment. This approach does not provide labels for detected obstacle but can rather be used as a region proposal algorithm for a classiﬁcation network. The study presented in [12] uses FCN trained on datasets that do not contain agricultural speciﬁc images and classes, ImageNet and Pascal-Context datasets. The proposed topology for encoder network corresponds to the ﬁrst 13 convolutional layers of VGG16 network. Therefore, it is possible to initialize the encoder net- work with pre-trained weights for large datasets. The encoder network is followed by the decoder network with the same number of convolutional layers. The ﬁnal soft-max layer produces class probabilities for each pixel independently. Each encoder layer in the network consists of convolu- tions, batch normalization and ReLU non-linearity, followed by non-overlapping max-pooling layer (2 × 2 window and stride 2).
